sentences.text: By it, the appellant has been convicted under Sections 363, 366 & 376(2) of IPC and Section 5 read with Section 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced accordingly.

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
According to the prosecution case, on 03.10.2019 at 5:00 p.m., the applicant enticed the victim, a young girl of four years, and committed sexual assault upon her.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that it is a case of non-identification of the applicant.
He referred to the statement of PW1-the victim, particularly, the questions when the victim was asked about the identification of the applicant and she nodded her head.

Reference has been made to two such questions and, in both the questions, the answer was by nodding head and, in one answer, the court had particularly recorded that the reply is 'No', but it is by nodding the head.

sentences.text: Based on it, it is argued that 'nodding the head' means 'No'.

In addition, it is also argued that,
according to PW2-the mother of the victim, for the first time, the victim was asked by her uncle (Jeth of this witness) but that person has not been examined as a witness.

It is also argued that,
according to the prosecution case, the appellant took the victim in a shop so as to give her toffee etc.,
but the shopkeeper has not been examined.
5. Learned counsel for the State submits that not only the victim, but PW3-the sister of the victim has also categorically identified the appellant.
6. It is the stage of the bail.
Post conviction the applicant does not have the benefit of presumption of innocence, because he is a convict.
Whatever the discussion has been made that shall confine to disposal of the bail application and it shall not be used for any other purposes.
7. The FIR is by name of the applicant.
He is not a stranger.
The victim has stated that he is her uncle (Tau).
He is the visitor of the victim's family.

The victim, in her examination, has, in fact,
named the appellant by name.

At one stage, she was asked as to whether she identifies the appellant,
she nodded her head.
It does not mean that she did not identify the appellant.
Moreover, PW3-the sister of the victim has also identified the appellant.
8. Having considered, this Court is of the view that there is no ground to enlarge the appellant/applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application of the appellant/applicant deserves to be rejected.
9. The bail application is rejected.
10. List this case on 11.03.2026 for hearing.

(Alok Mahra, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
